dct_description_sm:
Sub-Area + Neighbourhood Plan Completion | Squamish Community Dashboard

This indicator tracks the number of completed sub-area neighbourhood plans adopted by the District of Squamish in the reporting year. Sub-area plans are detailed plans for a defined area in the Official Community Plan (OCP) that apply to an existing (or future) neighbourhood or group of neighbourhoods. Where designated, sub-area plans are required prior to major new development to identify and develop a comprehensive plan for land use, density, environmental protection, neighbourhood design, transportation, municipal servicing and public amenities. 

About this target:

Seven existing sub-areas have been identified in the Squamish2040 OCP for neighbourhood planning (Schedule C) to be initiated over time. One sub-area or neighbourhood plan is completed every two years, or as resources allow. The District set intention to undertake and complete a sub-area planning for two residential neighbourhoods by 2022 (Loggers East and Garibaldi Estates, or other neighbourhood) per Council's Strategic Plan.

Analysis:

No Sub-Area Plans were initiated nor adopted in 2022-2024. In Spring 2021, the District initiated the Garibaldi Estates Neighbourhood Plan process, which continued through 2024 and is anticipated to be completed mid-2025. Expanded engagement as well as required integration of new provincial housing legislation necessitated additional time for plan development, review and finalization. In 2019, the District initiated Loggers East neighbourhood planning and the final plan was adopted by Council on February 23, 2020. Following the OCP adoption, in 2018 the Wilson Crescent neighbourhood 'micro-plan' was developed and endorsed by the District of Squamish. This leaves four other identified neighbourhood plan areas for future completion.

Reason for monitoring:

Sub-area and neighbourhood planning guides land use and development in existing developed areas over time to support complete, connected and livable neighbourhoods that offer housing diversity, access to nature, parklands, services and amenities for residents to thrive.
